01 Project Overview

This document records a hands-on Microsoft 365 administration lab, built to practise the tasks an IT support technician handles every day: provisioning users, managing licences, organising groups, securing sign-in, configuring Exchange and SharePoint, applying Intune policies, and monitoring service health. Every step was performed in a live trial tenant and screenshotted as it was done.

Several real constraints surfaced along the way, including a CSV import rejection, a single-seat licence pool that cascaded into mailbox, group and SharePoint limitations, and Microsoft portal changes that differed from the lab guide. Each is documented with its cause and resolution.

Lab Inventory

TenantOlwamIT.onmicrosoft.com (Microsoft 365 Business Premium trial)
Licence pool1 × Microsoft 365 Business Premium with Copilot (single trial seat)
Accounts provisioned15 users: 5 created manually, 9 via CSV bulk import, 1 via a user template
DepartmentsIT, Finance, Sales, HR, Marketing, Legal
Admin centres usedMicrosoft 365 admin centre, Microsoft Entra admin centre, Exchange admin centre, SharePoint admin centre, Microsoft Intune admin centre

02 Module 1 — User Provisioning

1.1 Creating Users Manually

Began by manually adding 5 users with different job titles and departments (IT, Finance, Marketing, HR and Sales) to understand every field in the Add a user form.

1.2 Bulk Import via CSV

Downloaded Microsoft's CSV template and filled it with the next batch of users.

IssueDuring the bulk CSV import, Microsoft Admin Center rejected the file with the error “Email address incomplete or has invalid characters” for every row.
Root causeUnlike the manual Add a user form, which auto-appends the domain to the username, the bulk CSV import requires the full User Principal Name (UPN) in the Username column. The CSV only contained the prefix (for example lerato.khumalo).
ResolutionUpdated the Username column to include the full address (lerato.khumalo@OlwamIT.onmicrosoft.com), re-saved the file as CSV, and re-uploaded it.

1.3 User Template

Created the “IT Department New Hire” user template with the domain, password policy, location and licence settings pre-configured, then used it to provision Zanele Nkosi.

03 Module 2 — Licensing Management

With only one licence seat in the trial tenant, licensing became a practical exercise in licence pool management: freeing a seat from one account and reassigning it where it was needed.

04 Module 3 — Groups & Distribution Lists

3.1 Microsoft 365 Group

Created the “IT Team” Microsoft 365 group as Private. Microsoft 365 groups provide a shared workspace (Teams, SharePoint, Planner), and the Private setting ensures only approved IT staff can view internal conversations and files.

3.2 Security Group

Created the “Finance-Access” security group. Unlike Microsoft 365 groups, security groups are used primarily to manage access to resources such as SharePoint sites, files and applications. This group would be used to grant Finance staff access to sensitive financial data.

3.3 Distribution List

Created the “All Staff” distribution list (allstaff@OlwamIT.onmicrosoft.com).

IssueThe wizard blocked group creation with a “Please provide an owner” error.
Root causeThe admin account's only licence had been reallocated to Sipho Dlamini in Module 2, so the admin account had no Exchange Online mailbox and could not be added as an owner of a mail-enabled group.
ResolutionAssigned Sipho (the only licensed user) as owner to complete creation. Only Sipho could be added as a member because of the single-licence limit.

05 Module 4 — MFA & Conditional Access

Enabled Multi-Factor Authentication per user for Aisha Patel, Thandi Mokoena and Ethan Williams via the per-user MFA portal. This legacy method enforces MFA on a per-account basis.

Then verified the “Require MFA for All Users” Conditional Access policy in the Entra admin centre. The details confirm it is in Report-only mode, targets all users and all cloud apps, requires MFA as a grant control, and excludes the admin account to prevent accidental lockout during testing.

Key takeawayReport-only mode lets a policy be tested against real sign-ins without risk of locking anyone out. In production it would be switched to On once the sign-in logs confirm it behaves as expected.

06 Module 5 — Exchange Online & Mail Flow

5.1 Shared Mailbox

Created the “IT Support” shared mailbox (itsupport@OlwamIT.onmicrosoft.com).

Troubleshooting noteOnly Sipho Dlamini, the single licensed user, could be added as a member. The other users are unlicensed in this trial tenant, so they have no Exchange Online mailbox and cannot be added to mail-enabled objects. In production, Ryan Botha would be assigned a licence before being added.

5.2 Email Alias

Added the alias hr.manager@OlwamIT.onmicrosoft.com via the Exchange admin centre.

Troubleshooting noteThe lab guide intended this alias for Thandi Mokoena (HR Manager). Because Thandi is unlicensed she has no Exchange Online mailbox, so an alias could not be added to her. To demonstrate the workflow, the alias was added to Sipho Dlamini instead.

5.3 Message Trace

Ran a message trace for the last 48 hours. It returned three system-generated emails sent to the admin account, all with a Delivered status, confirming the tool's ability to monitor mail flow and verify delivery status, timestamps and sender/recipient details.

07 Module 6 — Admin Roles & Least Privilege

Assigned and removed administrator roles to demonstrate the principle of least privilege: users get only the specific administrative access they need to do their job.

Troubleshooting noteThe Billing administrator role was not in the default role list in the Microsoft 365 admin centre due to a recent UI update. The role was assigned instead through the Roles and administrators blade in the Microsoft Entra admin centre, which lists all built-in roles.
Key takeawayRemoving a role when someone changes position or leaves is as important as granting it. Stale administrative access is a standing security risk.

08 Module 7 — SharePoint

7.1 Site Configuration & Membership

Verified the IT Department SharePoint site: Team site template, URL /sites/itdep, and Private privacy so only authorised members have access.

Troubleshooting noteOnly Sipho Dlamini and James Okonkwo could be added as site members (alongside the admin). Ryan Botha and Zanele Nkosi are unlicensed, so they lack SharePoint Online access. This shows the direct dependency between Microsoft 365 licensing and SharePoint access.

7.2 Document Library & Permissions

Created the “IT Procedures” document library and uploaded the lab guide. The Manage Access pane confirms the file inherits permissions from the site: Can edit for IT Department Members and read-only for Visitors. Lerato Khumalo was then added to the Site visitors group with read-only (Can view) access through the SharePoint admin centre.

09 Module 8 — Microsoft Intune

Explored the Intune admin centre, which provides mobile device management (MDM) and mobile application management (MAM). The dashboard covers Devices, Apps, Endpoint security and Reports.

Compliance Policy

Created a Windows compliance policy named “Basic Security Compliance” enforcing BitLocker encryption, a minimum OS version (10.0.19041) and password requirements, assigned to All users. This ensures devices meet organisational security standards before they can access company resources.

Configuration Profile

Configured a “Block USB Storage” device restrictions profile, setting Removable storage to Block in the General category.

10 Module 9 — Monitoring & Reports

Service Health

Reviewed the Microsoft 365 Service health dashboard. The top screenshot shows services with active advisories or incidents (Exchange Online, Teams, Purview and the Microsoft 365 suite). The bottom shows services operating normally (SharePoint Online, Intune, OneDrive). This is the first place IT support should check when users report widespread issues: if Microsoft has an outage, no amount of local troubleshooting will fix it.

Usage Reports

The active users and email activity reports currently show no data, which is expected: usage reports take up to 48 hours to populate and the only licensed user had not yet generated activity. In production these reports show adoption trends, licence utilisation and inactive accounts.

11 Module 10 — Password Reset & Self-Service Reset

Admin Password Reset

Reset the password for David van Wyk, generating a temporary password and enforcing a change at next sign-in. Although David is unlicensed (no mailbox), the admin reset still applies to his Entra ID account, showing that identity management is independent of licence assignment. Password resets are the most common helpdesk task, so knowing this process is essential.

Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR)

Enabled SSPR for all users in Entra ID. Registration is required at sign-in, and the Authentication methods policy enables Microsoft Authenticator, SMS and Email OTP for all users, the modern methods that support SSPR.

Troubleshooting noteThe lab guide said to enable Email and Mobile phone under the legacy Password reset → Authentication methods page. That page now blocks saving unless legacy security questions are configured (which the page flags as retiring in March 2027). Microsoft has moved these settings to the separate Authentication methods policy page, which is the current best-practice configuration and the one used here.

12 Summary & Lessons Learned

Troubleshooting Log

CSV import rejectedBulk import needs the full UPN in the Username column, not just the prefix. Fixed the file and re-uploaded.
One-seat licence poolUnlicensed users cannot hold mailboxes, join mail-enabled groups or access SharePoint. This shaped the owner, shared mailbox, alias and site-membership steps.
Billing admin role missingNot listed in the Microsoft 365 admin centre after a UI update. Assigned it through the Entra admin centre instead.
SSPR legacy pageSaving was blocked by a legacy security-questions requirement. Configured the Authentication methods policy instead.
Empty usage reportsExpected on a new tenant. Reports take up to 48 hours to populate.

What this lab demonstrates

  • Provisioned users manually, in bulk by CSV and from a template, and diagnosed a bulk-import failure to its root cause
  • Managed a constrained licence pool: assigning, removing and reallocating seats, and tracing the knock-on effects on mailboxes, groups and SharePoint
  • Created and compared Microsoft 365, security and distribution groups
  • Applied per-user MFA and a Conditional Access policy in Report-only mode
  • Configured Exchange Online shared mailboxes and aliases, and traced mail flow with message trace
  • Applied least privilege by assigning and removing admin roles, including a workaround through the Entra admin centre
  • Built a SharePoint site and document library with role-based permissions
  • Created Intune compliance and device restriction policies
  • Checked service health, reviewed usage reports, and handled admin and self-service password resets
Key takeawayLicensing underpins nearly everything in Microsoft 365. Mailboxes, group membership and SharePoint access all depend on it, so when a user cannot reach something, checking their licence is one of the first things to do.
